Off-grid group tracking · In development

Your Circle. One Map. No cell service required.

Shepard is a local-first tracking system for the places cellular coverage stops. Keep up to eight people, pets, or pieces of gear visible on real offline maps — without a cellular plan, Wi‑Fi, or a monthly bill.

The Shepard system

A quiet link back to your group.

Every Nomad finds its own position and sends it over long-range radio. The Shepard gathers those positions and passes them to your phone. One compact system, built for the edge of coverage.

Nomad

Phone app

One offline map

  1. Nomad — the tracker

    Goes with your people, pets, or gear. GPS + LoRa, up to 8 per Shepard.

  2. Shepard — stays with you

    Carry it in a pocket, pack, or on a keychain. It receives Nomad locations over LoRa and forwards them to your phone over Bluetooth.

  3. Phone app — everyone in view

    See the whole group on one offline map. No cell signal needed.

Why Shepard

Built for the blank spots.

Shepard strips away the dependencies that make ordinary trackers fail off-grid — towers, accounts, data plans, and cloud services.

01

Works beyond cell coverage

GNSS establishes location. LoRa carries it across the group. Cellular and Wi‑Fi are never part of the tracking loop.

02

No monthly fees

You buy hardware, not another subscription. Core tracking remains available without a service plan.

03

Offline maps that are actually offline

Download regions before you leave. Your group stays on the map when data coverage disappears.

04

Local by design

No cloud login is required for core tracking. Your positions stay between the trackers, Shepard, and your phone.

05

One group, eight Nomads

Build the set that fits your outing: people, a pet, critical gear — any mix, under one Shepard.

06

Field-ready target

Compact rechargeable hardware, USB‑C power, and an IP67 enclosure target for real outdoor use.

Your people, in view

For groups that move together.

A family is not a dot. Neither is a trail crew, a campsite, or a dog that slipped a lead. Shepard is designed around the whole group.

01/ GROUPS

Keep the whole group on one map.

Track your hiking or camping party off-grid, even when there is no cell signal.

02/ KIDS

More room to explore.

See where everyone is at parks, camps, and festivals — without handing every child a phone.

03/ OLDER PARENTS

Stay connected outdoors.

A simple location link for family walks and outings where cellular coverage is patchy or absent.

04/ PETS

One more member of the group.

Clip a Nomad to a collar and follow the same map you use for everyone else.

FAQ

Before you head out.

The short answers on coverage, phones, fees, and what “coming soon” means.

No. Nomads use satellite navigation to determine location and LoRa to send it to the Shepard. The Shepard connects locally to your phone over Bluetooth.
No subscription is planned for core tracking. Shepard is being designed around hardware ownership and offline maps, not a required cloud service.
The phone provides the map and interface, while the Shepard provides the radio bridge to the Nomads. Keep the Shepard and phone with the group owner for the full map experience.
Range depends heavily on terrain, vegetation, height, and obstructions. Rather than publish a best-case number now, Shepard will share repeatable real-world field results after the production hardware is validated.
Not yet. The hardware and companion app are in development. Join the launch list to hear about field testing, availability, and final specifications.
